title.zh: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标
title.en: Volume 247 Biographies 34: Peng Ershu, Lu Zhenfen, Yao Yanzhu, Bi Zhenji, Fang Guodong, Yu Pengju, Wang Tianjian, Yue Tingbiao
title.raw: 卷247 列傳三十四 彭而述 陆振芬 姚延著 毕振姬 方国栋 于朋举 王天鑑 越廷标

sentences.zh: =彭而述=彭而述，字子籛，河南鄧州人。

translations.literal: Peng Ershu—courtesy name Zijie—was a native of Dengzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ershu, styled Zijie, came from Dengzhou in Henan Province.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎進士，官陽曲知縣，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, served as magistrate of Yangqu, and returned home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree under the Chongzhen Emperor, served as magistrate of Yangqu, and went into mourning after his mother died.

sentences.zh: 順治初，英親王徇湖廣，薦為提學僉事，遷永州道參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the Prince of Ying campaigned in Huguang, he recommended him as educational administration commissioner, and he was transferred to be Yongzhou circuit junior vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign, as the Prince of Ying prosecuted the campaign in Huguang, he recommended Peng for the post of educational administration commissioner; Peng was later promoted to junior vice prefect of the Yongzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 孔有德定湖南，薦而述授貴州巡撫，予兵三千以行。

translations.literal: When Kong Youde pacified Hunan, he recommended Ershu and appointed him governor of Guizhou, granting three thousand troops for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: After Kong Youde secured Hunan, he recommended Ershu for governor of Guizhou and gave him three thousand troops for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 次靖州，降將陳友龍叛，圍州城，而述夜開西門出，營山下，選勁騎乘霧衝陣，賊潰且走，副將賀進才戰死。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingzhou, the surrendered general Chen Youlong rebelled and besieged the prefectural city; Ershu opened the west gate at night and went out, encamped below the mountain, selected crack cavalry to charge the formation through the fog, the rebels were routed and fled, and Vice Commander He Jincai died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou the surrendered general Chen Youlong rebelled and besieged the city. Ershu slipped out through the west gate by night and camped below the hills, then sent picked horsemen charging through the mist; the rebels broke and fled, though Vice Commander He Jincai was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 城兵大噪，欲與友龍合，而述拔眾退守寶慶，告有德益師，與賊相持紫陽河上。

translations.literal: The soldiers in the city clamored loudly and wished to join with Youlong; Ershu led his forces away to defend Shaocheng, reported to Youde to send more troops, and faced off with the rebels along the Ziyang River.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison troops grew unruly and nearly joined Chen Youlong, but Ershu withdrew his men to hold Shaocheng, asked Youde for reinforcements, and locked in a stalemate with the rebels along the Ziyang River.

sentences.zh: 永州陷，劾免官。

translations.literal: When Yongzhou fell, he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongzhou fell he was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂徵水西土司安坤，而述謀曰：「烏蒙、烏撒、鎮雄、東川四府與水西為脣齒，土司隴安籓又與安氏婚媾。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui campaigned against the Shuixi chieftain An Kun, Ershu advised: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan are lip-and-teeth with Shuixi, and the chieftain Long Anfan is also allied by marriage with the An clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui marched against the Shuixi chieftain An Kun, Ershu urged him: "The four prefectures of Wumeng, Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Dongchuan stand shoulder to shoulder with Shuixi, and the chieftain Long Anfan has marriage ties with the An family.

sentences.zh: 今四府雖名內附，狼子野心，勢必顧惜其種類。

translations.literal: Though the four prefectures now bear the name of submission to the interior, they have wolfish hearts and wild ambitions and will surely look after their own kind.
translations.idiomatic: Although those four prefectures are nominally under imperial control, their rulers remain fiercely tribal-minded and will surely shield their kin.

sentences.zh: 以水西之強，而安籓與四府附之，安坤未易制也。

translations.literal: Given Shuixi's strength, and with Anfan and the four prefectures attached to it, An Kun will not be easy to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: With Shuixi so strong and Long Anfan and the four prefectures rallying to it, An Kun will not be easily subdued.

sentences.zh: 莫如先定四府，馘安籓，然後西南可無患。

translations.literal: Better first to pacify the four prefectures and cut off Anfan, and then the southwest may be free of trouble.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to secure the four prefectures first and eliminate Long Anfan; only then can the southwest be kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 」三桂用其策，誅安坤。

translations.literal: Sangui adopted his strategy and executed An Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui took his advice and put An Kun to death.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西右布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be right administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 三桂薦為雲南左布政使，而述乞歸，三桂留之，會有詔召，遂行，出會城三十里，一夕無疾卒。

translations.literal: Sangui recommended him as left administration commissioner of Yunnan; Ershu begged to retire, Sangui detained him, then an imperial summons came and he set out; thirty li beyond Kunming he died suddenly in one night without prior illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui recommended him for Left Administration Commissioner of Yunnan. Ershu asked to go home, but Sangui kept him there until an imperial summons arrived and he set out. Thirty li beyond the provincial capital he died suddenly in the night, without any known illness.

sentences.zh: =陸振芬=陸振芬，字令遠，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhenfen—courtesy name Lingyuan—was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfen, styled Lingyuan, was from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Shunzhi (1649).

sentences.zh: 時兩粵未平，廷議破格用人，即新進士中遴才除道府。

translations.literal: At the time the two Guang provinces were not yet pacified; the court discussed using men outside the usual rules and selecting talented new jinshi for circuit and prefectural posts.
translations.idiomatic: With Guangdong and Guangxi still unsettled, the court decided to appoint men outside the usual channels and chose the most capable new jinshi for circuit and prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 振芬授廣東惠潮道副使，從師南征。

translations.literal: Zhenfen was appointed vice commissioner of the Huichao circuit in Guangdong and followed the army south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen was made Vice Commissioner of the Huichao Circuit in Guangdong and marched south with the army.

sentences.zh: 是冬，克南雄。

translations.literal: That winter they captured Nanxiong.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the forces took Nanxiong.

sentences.zh: 七年春，度大庾嶺，次韶州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed Dayuling and halted at Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year they crossed the Dayu Pass and made camp at Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 韶州以南望風降，進規會城，既下，振芬與總兵郭虎率師赴惠州，剿撫歸善、海豐諸寨。

translations.literal: South of Shaozhou the cities surrendered at the report of their approach; advancing to invest Guangzhou, once it fell Zhenfen with Commander Guo Hu led troops to Huizhou to subdue and pacify the stockades of Guishan, Haifeng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: South of Shaozhou cities submitted as the army advanced; after Guangzhou fell, Zhenfen and Commander Guo Hu marched on Huizhou to pacify the fortified villages of Guishan, Haifeng, and the surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 將至，諸寨窺兵寡，出拒。

translations.literal: As they were about to arrive, the stockades saw that the troops were few and came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: As they approached, the stockades saw how few troops they had and came out to fight.

sentences.zh: 振芬選精銳數百人繞出其旁擊之，獲一隊，諸寨皆懼。

translations.literal: Zhenfen selected several hundred elite troops to circle around and strike them from the flank, captured one unit, and all the stockades were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen picked several hundred crack troops to flank them, captured one band, and every stockade grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 於是諭以禍福，降者踵至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he instructed them on fortune and calamity, and those who surrendered came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained what submission or resistance would bring, and surrendering parties arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 至海豐，守者抗不下。

translations.literal: At Haifeng the defenders resisted and the place could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: At Haifeng the defenders held out and the city would not yield.

sentences.zh: 振芬與虎駐五坡驛，他將自羊氾嶺會師合攻之，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Zhenfen and Hu encamped at Wupo Post; another general joined forces from Yangfan Ridge for a combined assault, and they then captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen and Guo Hu camped at Wupo Post while another column came down from Yangfan Ridge; the combined attack finally took the city.

sentences.zh: 碣石衛亦降。

translations.literal: Jieshi Guard also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshi Guard surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 八年，抵潮州，上官，聯結諸鎮，檢制土官，招集流亡，簡省徭役，民始有更生之樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou, reported to his superiors, linked the various garrisons, restrained native officials, gathered the displaced, simplified corvée and levies, and the people first knew the joy of renewed life.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he reached Chaozhou, took up his post, coordinated the garrison towns, kept native officials in check, gathered refugees, and cut back levies so that people at last felt they could live again.

sentences.zh: 亂甫定，用法嚴，郡縣輒濫禁無辜。

translations.literal: The turmoil had just settled; the law was applied strictly, and prefectures and counties often detained innocents without cause.
translations.idiomatic: With the fighting barely over, strict enforcement swept the region, and local officials often jailed innocent people on slight suspicion.

sentences.zh: 振芬與屬吏約，期五十日清庶獄，囹圄為空。

translations.literal: Zhenfen made an agreement with his subordinates to clear ordinary cases within fifty days, and the prisons were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen pledged to his staff that every ordinary case would be cleared within fifty days, and soon the jails stood empty.

sentences.zh: 九年，會師復平遠，總兵郝尚久故降將，陰持兩端，聞將改授水師副總兵，結山海諸寇僭立帥府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year united forces recovered Pingyuan; Commander Hao Shangjiu, a former surrendered general, secretly kept to a double game; hearing he was to be reassigned as vice commander of the naval forces, he joined coastal and mountain bandits and presumptuously set up a command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the combined army retook Pingyuan. Commander Hao Shangjiu, once a surrendered Ming general, had long played both sides; when he heard he would be reassigned to the navy, he joined coastal and mountain bandits and set up a rebel headquarters.

sentences.zh: 振芬牒大吏策弭變，不應。

translations.literal: Zhenfen memorialized the high officials with a plan to quell the disturbance, but they did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen sent urgent dispatches to his superiors outlining how to head off the revolt, but no action was taken.

sentences.zh: 十年春，尚久自署新泰侯，舉兵圍道署。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Shangjiu styled himself Marquis of Xintai and raised troops to besiege the circuit office.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Hao styled himself Marquis of Xintai and marched on Zhenfen's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 振芬諭以大義，不從，使告變。

translations.literal: Zhenfen admonished him with the greater principle of duty, but he would not listen; Zhenfen sent word to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenfen appealed to him on grounds of loyalty, but Hao refused to listen, so Zhenfen reported the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 秋，固山兵至，振芬約為內應，引外兵入，誅尚久。

translations.literal: In autumn the banner troops arrived; Zhenfen arranged to act as inner collaborator, led the outside troops in, and executed Shangjiu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn banner troops arrived; Zhenfen arranged an inside rendezvous, brought the relief force in, and Hao Shangjiu was killed.

sentences.zh: 事平，引疾歸里。

translations.literal: When the matter was settled, he cited illness and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he pleaded illness and retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 家居四十年乃卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for forty years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for forty years before he died.

sentences.zh: =姚延著=姚延著，字象懸，浙江烏程人。

translations.literal: Yao Yanzhu—courtesy name Xiangxuan—was a native of Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanzhu, styled Xiangxuan, was from Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，除廣西慶遠知府。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi and was appointed prefect of Qingyuan in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 從師南征，調柳州，有守禦功，又調平樂。

translations.literal: He followed the army south on campaign, was transferred to Liuzhou where he had merit in defense, and was then transferred to Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in the south, was transferred to Liuzhou where he distinguished himself in defense, and later to Pingle.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東嶺南道副使，撫僮寨，擢江南按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Lingnan circuit in Guangdong, pacified Yao stockades, and was elevated to Jiangnan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Lingnan Circuit in Guangdong, pacified Zhuang stockades, and was later made Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鄭成功內犯，陷鎮江，入攻江寧。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong invaded inland, captured Zhenjiang, and advanced to attack Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong struck inland, took Zhenjiang, and pressed on toward Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 延著佐總督郎廷佐繕守備，安輯危城，閭閻不擾。

translations.literal: Yanzhu assisted Governor Lang Tingzuo in preparing defenses, pacified the endangered city, and the neighborhoods were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu helped Governor Lang Tingzuo ready the city's defenses, kept order in the threatened capital, and left ordinary neighborhoods largely undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 民間時有羊尾黨，事發，株連數百人。

translations.literal: From time to time there was a Yangwei Party among the people; when the affair broke, several hundred were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: A secret group known as the Yangwei Party had operated among the people; when the case broke, hundreds were swept up by association.

sentences.zh: 延著謂廷佐曰：「寇在門，不可興大獄、搖人心。

translations.literal: Yanzhu said to Tingzuo: "The enemy is at the gate; one must not launch a great prosecution and shake the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu told Tingzuo, "The enemy is at our gates—we must not launch a sweeping prosecution and unsettle the populace."

sentences.zh: 」獄乃解。

translations.literal: The prosecution was then loosened.
translations.idiomatic: The mass trial was called off.

sentences.zh: 當事急，人多疑貳，民間有宿怨，輒誣以通敵。

translations.literal: When affairs were urgent many people harbored doubts; where there were old grudges among the people, they were often falsely accused of communicating with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis many grew suspicious of their neighbors, and old feuds led to accusations of collusion with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 延著嚴治反坐，多所全活。

translations.literal: Yanzhu strictly punished those who framed others in retaliation, and many lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu cracked down hard on false accusers and thereby saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 城民有升高而望者，邏者執之，總管喀喀木以為敵諜，延著力爭，得不死。

translations.literal: A city resident climbed high to look out; patrolmen seized him, Superintendent Kekemu took him for an enemy spy, and Yanzhu argued forcefully so that he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When a townsman climbed a height to look out, patrolmen seized him and Superintendent Kekemu declared him a spy; Yanzhu argued strenuously and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木部兵擾城市，延著捕得械斃之。

translations.literal: Kekemu's troops harassed the city; Yanzhu captured them and had them bound and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers under Kekemu were plundering the city; Yanzhu seized the culprits and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 吏卒私掠被難婦女，延著親駐江乾，召其家，遣還者一千七百人，以此忤喀喀木。

translations.literal: Clerks and soldiers privately seized women afflicted by the disaster; Yanzhu personally stationed himself on the riverbank, summoned their families, and sent back seventeen hundred persons; for this he offended Kekemu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and soldiers were seizing women made refugees by the fighting; Yanzhu went in person to the riverbank, called their families forward, and restored seventeen hundred women—an act that deeply offended Kekemu.

sentences.zh: 事定敘功，擢河南左布政使。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled merits were reckoned and he was promoted to left administration commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the crisis he was rewarded for his service and promoted to Left Administration Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 旋以憂歸，而金壇獄起。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on mourning leave, and then the Jintan case arose.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to mourn his parents, and then the notorious Jintan case erupted.

sentences.zh: 鎮江之陷也，屬縣戒嚴。

translations.literal: When Zhenjiang fell, the subordinate counties went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenjiang fell, the surrounding counties were placed under martial law.

sentences.zh: 金壇知縣任體坤集縣中士大夫王重、袁大受等謀遣諸生十輩詣鎮江乞緩兵。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Jintan, Ren Tikun, gathered the gentry of the county such as Wang Chong and Yuan Dashou and plotted to send ten groups of students to Zhenjiang to beg for a truce.
translations.idiomatic: Jintan's magistrate Ren Tikun joined local notables Wang Chong and Yuan Dashou in a plan to send ten parties of students to Zhenjiang to plead for a ceasefire.

sentences.zh: 丹徒亂民王再興兵起，復令書吏、耆民數十人送款，盡竊庫帑以遁。

translations.literal: Wang Zai, a rebel from Dantu, raised troops; they again ordered dozens of clerks and elders to deliver surrender, stole all the treasury funds, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dantu rebel Wang Zai rose in arms, Ren again sent dozens of clerks and elders to offer surrender—and emptied the county treasury before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 喀喀木等擊敗成功，體坤乃復至縣，賂重、大受謁大吏，謂士民送款，冀掩棄城罪。

translations.literal: When Kekemu and others defeated Chenggong, Tikun then returned to the county, bribed Chong and Dashou to call on high officials, and claimed the gentry and people had sent surrender, hoping to cover his crime of abandoning the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Kekemu and others routed Zheng Chenggong, Tikun returned to his post and bribed Wang Chong and Yuan Dashou to tell superiors that the local elite had negotiated surrender, hoping to hide his own desertion of the county.

sentences.zh: 重、大受居鄉多不法，為諸生所撓。

translations.literal: Chong and Dashou had committed many unlawful acts while living in the countryside and were obstructed by the students.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong and Yuan Dashou had long bullied the countryside until the local students stood up to them.

sentences.zh: 至是欲以叛坐諸生，泄私怨，列姓名以上。

translations.literal: At this juncture they wished to charge the students with rebellion to vent private grievances and listed names to submit upward.
translations.idiomatic: Now they sought revenge by charging the students with treason and submitted lists of names to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 巡按馬勝聲疏聞，下廷佐令延著鞫其獄。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Shengsheng memorialized report, and the case was sent down to Tingzuo ordering Yanzhu to try the prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Ma Shengsheng reported the matter, and Lang Tingzuo was ordered to have Yanzhu investigate.

sentences.zh: 延著縶縣吏李鍾秀，訊得實，欲但坐體坤，餘皆減罪。

translations.literal: Yanzhu detained the county clerk Li Zhongxiu, examined and got the facts, and wished to punish only Tikun while reducing the offenses of the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu arrested county clerk Li Zhongxiu, uncovered the truth, and sought to punish only Ren Tikun while mitigating charges against the others.

sentences.zh: 大受騰書京師為蜚語，欲並陷延著，御史馮班發其狀。

translations.literal: Dashou sent secret letters to the capital spreading rumors, intending to entangle Yanzhu as well; Censor Feng Ban exposed the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Dashou sent inflammatory reports to the capital hoping to implicate Yanzhu as well, but Censor Feng Ban exposed the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎尼滿奉詔勘提督馬逢知獄，命即訊，乃坐重、大受及諸士大夫集議者。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister Niman was ordered by imperial edict to investigate the case of Governor-General Ma Fengzhi and was commanded to try immediately; thereupon Chong, Dashou, and the various gentry who had met to deliberate were convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Niman had been sent to investigate another case and was ordered to take this one immediately; Wang Chong, Yuan Dashou, and the gentry who had joined the deliberations were all convicted.

sentences.zh: 諸生及書吏、耆民送款者皆斬，體坤以被逼迫減為絞。

translations.literal: The students and the clerks and elders who had delivered surrender were all beheaded; Tikun, on grounds of having been compelled, had his sentence reduced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: The students and the clerks and elders who had negotiated surrender were all executed; Ren Tikun, deemed to have acted under duress, received the reduced sentence of strangulation.

sentences.zh: 巡按何可化又疏劾延著讞從叛罪人史記青、管得勝傅輕比，又有王天福、韓王錫並縱不擬罪，與金壇獄並論，亦坐絞。

translations.literal: Censor He Kehua again memorialized impeaching Yanzhu for lenient sentencing of the rebel convicts Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng Fu, and also for Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi being released without proposed punishment; taken together with the Jintan case, he too was sentenced to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector He Kehua further accused Yanzhu of leniency toward alleged rebels Shi Jiqing and Guan Desheng, and of releasing Wang Tianfu and Han Wangxi without charge; grouping these with the Jintan case, Yanzhu too was sentenced to death by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 時喀喀木主軍事，新破敵，尤威重，素不慊於延著。

translations.literal: At the time Kekemu directed military affairs, had newly defeated the enemy, and was especially formidable; he had long been displeased with Yanzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Kekemu then commanded the armies, fresh from victory and at the height of his influence, and had long borne a grudge against Yanzhu.

sentences.zh: 民間謂延著之死，喀喀木實主之。

translations.literal: Among the people it was said that Yanzhu's death was in fact orchestrated by Kekemu.
translations.idiomatic: Popular rumor held that Kekemu was really behind Yanzhu's execution.

sentences.zh: 就刑日，江寧為罷市，士民哭踴。

translations.literal: On the day of execution Jiangning observed a market strike; gentry and common people wept and stamped in grief.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was executed Nanjing shut down its markets; scholars and commoners wept and stamped their feet in grief.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，數百里祭奠不絕，建祠雞鳴山下私祀焉。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, for several hundred li offerings of mourning did not cease; a shrine was built below Jiming Hill for private veneration.
translations.idiomatic: As his coffin traveled home, mourners lined the route for hundreds of li, and a private shrine was erected for him below Jiming Hill.

sentences.zh: 子淳燾，康熙六年進士，授內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: His son Chunyi became a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed a Secretariat drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunyi passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed a drafting officer in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 伏闕上書為延著訟冤。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial to plead Yanzhu's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt at the palace gate and submitted a memorial pleading his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 累擢湖廣提學道僉事，坐事罷，未行，值叛卒夏逢龍之亂，誓死不為屈。

translations.literal: He rose through promotions to educational administration commissioner of Huguang, was dismissed for an affair before he had set out, and encountered the revolt of the mutinous soldier Xia Fenglong; he vowed he would die rather than submit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Educational Administration Commissioner of Huguang, but was dismissed before taking up the post; when the mutineer Xia Fenglong rebelled, he swore he would die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 事聞，复官，授岳常澧道副使。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was restored to office and appointed vice prefect of the Yuechangli circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his conduct he was reinstated and appointed Vice Prefect of the Yuechangli Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: =畢振姬=畢振姬，字亮四，山西高平人。

translations.literal: Bi Zhenji—courtesy name Liangsi—was a native of Gaoping in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhenji, styled Liangsi, was from Gaoping in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授平陽教授。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed instructor of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed instructor at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy and was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as an assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy and eventually rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 曹事暇，獨坐陋室，布被瓦盆，讀書不稍倦。

translations.literal: When he had leisure from his duties he sat alone in a shabby room with a cloth quilt and earthen bowl, reading without the slightest weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare hours he would sit alone in a bare room furnished with nothing but a cotton quilt and a clay bowl, reading without tiring.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為山東濟南道參議。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he went out to serve as junior vice prefect of the Jinan circuit in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was posted as Junior Vice Prefect of the Jinan Circuit in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，流民踞山谷為盜，振姬晝夜馳三百里往諭之，悉就撫，全活者七​​千餘人。

translations.literal: In a drought year displaced persons occupied valleys and mountains as bandits; Zhenji traveled three hundred li day and night to instruct them, and all submitted to pacification—more than seven thousand lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year refugees had turned bandit in the hills; Zhenji rode three hundred li without rest to reason with them, brought them all back to loyalty, and saved more than seven thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 泰山香稅，歲羨餘七千金，例充公使錢，振姬悉以佐餉。

translations.literal: The Taishan incense tax yearly yielded a surplus of seven thousand taels of gold, which by precedent supplied public mission funds; Zhenji applied all of it to support army rations.
translations.idiomatic: The Taishan incense tax produced an annual surplus of seven thousand taels, normally reserved for official missions; Zhenji diverted all of it to army provisions.

sentences.zh: 調廣東驛傳道僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be commissioner of the courier and relay circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Courier Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時三籓使命往來絡繹，胥吏乘以私派折價，民苦之，振姬一繩以法，閱數月，減船數百，減​​費七萬有奇。

translations.literal: At the time the missions of the Three Feudatories came and went in continuous streams; clerks took advantage to make private requisitions at discounted rates, and the people suffered; Zhenji applied the law uniformly on a single standard; within several months he reduced boats by several hundred and cut expenses by more than seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With the Three Feudatories constantly sending envoys, clerks extorted kickbacks through corrupt pricing and the people groaned under the burden; Zhenji enforced the law strictly, and within months cut hundreds of boats from the fleet and saved more than seventy thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 調浙江金衢嚴道參政，擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administrator of the Jinquyan circuit in Zhejiang and was elevated to surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of the Jinquyan Circuit in Zhejiang and later Surveillance Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 所至以廉能聞。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he served he won a reputation for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣布政使，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to administration commissioner of Huguang and begged leave on grounds of illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administration Commissioner of Huguang but soon asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，詔舉博學鴻儒，左都御史魏裔介、副都御史劉楗疏薦之。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign an edict summoned erudite scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign the throne called for eminent scholars; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jian both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命廷臣舉清廉吏，裔介复疏言：「振姬清操絕世，才略過人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the court was ordered to nominate honest officials; Yijie again memorialized saying: "Zhenji's purity of conduct is unmatched in the age, and his talent and strategy surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the court was instructed to nominate honest officials; Wei Yijie wrote again: "Zhenji's integrity is unrivaled, and his talent extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 請告十餘年，躬耕百畝，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: He has been on leave for more than ten years, personally cultivating a hundred mu, reading without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He has been retired more than ten years, farming a hundred mu with his own hands and never ceasing his studies."

sentences.zh: 」楗亦言：「振姬居官不染一塵。

translations.literal: Jian also said: "In office Zhenji never touched a speck of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian added: "In office Zhenji never stained his hands with the slightest corruption.

sentences.zh: 歸日一僕一馬，了無長物，真學行兼優之人。

translations.literal: On the day he returned, one servant and one horse—he had nothing in excess—a man truly combining learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he had but one servant and one horse and no possessions to speak of—a man of true learning and character."

sentences.zh: 」下部議，以振姬老，置勿用。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to ministries for deliberation; because Zhenji was old, he was set aside and not employed.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries deliberated and, finding Zhenji too old, set the nomination aside.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: =方國棟=方國棟，字幹霄，順天宛平人。

translations.literal: Fang Guodong—courtesy name Ganxiao—was a native of Wanping in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guodong, styled Ganxiao, was from Wanping in the Shuntian metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 順治三年舉人，授蠡縣教諭。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed instructor of Lixian.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed county instructor at Lixian.

sentences.zh: 入為國子監助教，累擢至刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy and was repeatedly promoted to director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the capital as an Imperial Academy assistant instructor and eventually rose to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為廣東海北道僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he went out to serve as commissioner of the Haibei circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was posted as Commissioner of the Haibei Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 海寇鄧耀居島中，時出剽掠。

translations.literal: The sea bandit Deng Yao dwelt on an island and from time to time came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The pirate Deng Yao lived on an offshore island and raided the coast whenever he could.

sentences.zh: 國棟以三千人分五道進剿，檄鄰道出兵扼要隘，擒耀，解散餘黨。

translations.literal: Guodong with three thousand men divided into five columns advanced to suppress him, ordered neighboring circuits to send troops to hold key passes, captured Yao, and dispersed the remainder of the band.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong led three thousand men in five columns, ordered neighboring districts to block the passes, captured Deng Yao, and dispersed his followers.

sentences.zh: 事平，雷、廉兩部諸富人為賊所誣，械系者眾，國棟察其冤，為辨雪。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, in the Lei and Lian departments many wealthy men had been framed by bandits and a great many were shackled and detained; Guodong discerned their innocence and cleared them.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign many wealthy men in Leizhou and Lianzhou had been framed by the bandits and imprisoned in large numbers; Guodong saw they were innocent and cleared them.

sentences.zh: 諸富人裒千金為報，國棟曰：「吾憫若無辜，柰何污我？

translations.literal: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels in gold as a reward; Guodong said: "I pity your innocence—how can you stain me?
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy men pooled a thousand taels as a gift; Guodong said, "I pitied your innocence—how could you try to bribe me?"

sentences.zh: 」卻之。

translations.literal: He refused it.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the gift.

sentences.zh: 遷山西寧武道參議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be junior vice prefect of the Ningwu circuit in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Junior Vice Prefect of the Ningwu Circuit in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年裁缺，改江南蘇松常道參議。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi his post was abolished; he was reassigned as junior vice prefect of the Susongchang circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was abolished in the sixth year of Kangxi, he was reassigned as Junior Vice Prefect of the Susongchang Circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 太湖堤岸傾圮，率吏民修葺，修沿海墩台及吳淞、劉河兩徬，工費不擾民。

translations.literal: The dikes of Taihu collapsed; he led clerks and people to repair them, restored coastal watch towers and the two dykes of Wusong and Liuhe, and the labor costs did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihu dikes gave way he led officials and people to rebuild them, restored coastal watchtowers and the Wusong and Liuhe embankments, and did all of it without burdening the populace.

sentences.zh: 師下閩、粵，徵調旁午，國棟一意與民休息，每遇急徵，從容部署。

translations.literal: When the army descended on Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions came in rapid succession; Guodong devoted himself entirely to letting the people rest, and whenever urgent levies arose he deployed resources at an unhurried pace.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial armies marched on Fujian and Guangdong, requisitions piled up one after another; Guodong focused on giving the people respite, and whenever urgent levies came he organized supplies calmly.

sentences.zh: 芻茭糧糗，預儲以待，軍興無乏，閭左晏然。

translations.literal: Fodder and dry rations were stored in advance to await use; when the army mobilized there was no shortage, and the neighborhoods were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled fodder and grain in advance, so that armies never went wanting and neighborhoods stayed at peace.

sentences.zh: 戒屬吏無朘民，郡縣稍稍知斂戢，不敢事剝削。

translations.literal: He warned subordinate officials not to scrape from the people; prefectures and counties gradually knew to restrain themselves and dared not practice extortion.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade his staff to squeeze the people, and county officials gradually learned restraint and stopped their extortions.

sentences.zh: 連歲用兵，度支不給，詔各省籌裕餉之策。

translations.literal: For successive years troops were employed and the revenue bureau could not meet expenses; an edict ordered each province to devise plans for plentiful military funds.
translations.idiomatic: Years of warfare had drained the treasury, and the throne ordered every province to propose ways to secure adequate military revenue.

sentences.zh: 國棟言：「古今生財之說，開與節二者而已。

translations.literal: Guodong said: "From ancient times to the present the theories of generating wealth amount only to two—expansion and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong argued, "Throughout history the ways to generate revenue boil down to two: expanding income and cutting costs."

sentences.zh: 議開於今日，已無可加，當議節，自朝廷始。

translations.literal: To discuss expansion today—there is nothing more that can be added; one should discuss frugality, beginning with the court itself.
translations.idiomatic: "To expand revenue today there is nothing left to add; we must discuss thrift, and it must begin at court."

sentences.zh: 舊制，江南歲市布五萬匹供宮府賚予，宜可罷，歲省帑金三萬。

translations.literal: By the old regulation Jiangnan yearly purchased fifty thousand bolts of cloth to supply palace grants and rewards; this may properly be abolished, yearly saving thirty thousand taels from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: "Under the old system Jiangnan bought fifty thousand bolts of cloth annually for palace gifts—that custom should be abolished, saving thirty thousand taels a year."

sentences.zh: 」議上，報可，滿洲兵駐防蘇州，議築營舍於王府基，當城中。

translations.literal: The proposal was submitted and approved; Manchu troops were garrisoned at Suzhou, and it was proposed to build barracks on the site of a princely mansion, in the center of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted. When Manchu troops were stationed at Suzhou, officials proposed building barracks on a former princely residence in the heart of the city.

sentences.zh: 國棟以兵民雜居難久安，持不可，乃改營南城隙地，民便之。

translations.literal: Guodong held that soldiers and civilians living mixed together could not long endure in peace and insisted it could not be done; thereupon barracks were moved to vacant land in the southern city, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong argued that mixing troops and civilians could not last and objected firmly; the barracks were moved to open ground in the southern suburbs instead, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 宜興善權山中寺僧與豪族爭地，聚眾焚寺殺僧，知縣告亂，大吏將發兵。

translations.literal: At Shanchuan in Yixing, monks of a temple and a powerful clan disputed land; they gathered a crowd, burned the temple, and killed monks; the magistrate reported disorder, and high officials were about to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shanchuan hills of Yixing, temple monks and a powerful clan fought over land; the mob burned the temple and killed monks. The magistrate reported a rebellion, and superiors prepared to send troops.

sentences.zh: 國棟單騎馳往，得首禍寘法，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Guodong rode alone at speed to the scene, secured the chief culprits and placed them under the law, and questioned no one else.
translations.idiomatic: Guodong rode there alone, arrested the ringleaders and punished them, and took no action against anyone else.

sentences.zh: 吳俗健訟，喜投缿告密，國棟輒不問，即有所案，亦從寬。

translations.literal: Wu custom was vigorous in litigation and fond of dropping accusation boxes to inform secretly; Guodong generally did not inquire, and even when there was a case he acted leniently.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu were famously litigious and fond of anonymous denunciations; Guodong routinely ignored them, and even when he took up a case he leaned toward leniency.

sentences.zh: 馭吏嚴，而拊循士民具有恩意。

translations.literal: He controlled officials strictly, yet in comforting scholars and common people he was full of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was strict with his staff yet considerate and generous toward scholars and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year (1659).

sentences.zh: 吳民思之，建祠虎丘山麓以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Wu missed him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill to venerate him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu mourned him and built a shrine at the foot of Tiger Hill in his honor.

sentences.zh: =於朋舉=於朋舉，字襄子，江南金壇人。

translations.literal: Yu Pengju—courtesy name Xiangzi—was a native of Jintan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pengju, styled Xiangzi, was from Jintan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was transferred to Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and upon graduating was appointed a revising compiler.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為河南睢陳道副使，政不擾民。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as vice commissioner of the Suichen circuit in Henan; his administration did not trouble the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as Vice Commissioner of the Suichen Circuit in Henan and governed without harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 郾城盜殺縣官而逸，士民洶洶，謂城將受屠。

translations.literal: At Yancheng bandits killed the county magistrate and fled; gentry and people were in uproar, saying the city was about to be massacred.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits in Yancheng killed the magistrate and fled, the populace panicked, fearing the city would be put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 朋舉馳至，撫諭毋恐。

translations.literal: Pengju rode at speed to the place and comforted them with instruction, telling them not to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju hurried there and reassured them not to be afraid.

sentences.zh: 營將以兵至，拒不使入城。

translations.literal: The garrison commander was about to bring troops; he refused and would not let them enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: When a garrison commander marched troops toward the city, he barred them from entering.

sentences.zh: 大吏召朋舉詰責，對曰：「郾城令，朋舉婦翁也。

translations.literal: High officials summoned Pengju to reprimand him; he replied: "The magistrate of Yancheng is Pengju's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors summoned him to account for himself; he answered, "The magistrate of Yancheng was my father-in-law."

sentences.zh: 豈不欲甘心是盜？

translations.literal: Would he not wish to have his satisfaction on those bandits?
translations.idiomatic: "Do you think I did not want those bandits brought to justice?"

sentences.zh: 獨柰何苦良民！

translations.literal: Only how can one make the good people suffer!
translations.idiomatic: "But why visit suffering on innocent people?"

sentences.zh: 」大吏悟，止兵，亦得盜正其罪。

translations.literal: The high officials understood, halted the troops, and also got the bandits punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: His superiors understood, halted the troops, and the bandits were duly punished by law.

sentences.zh: 遷福建福寧道參政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be administrator of the Funing circuit in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of the Funing Circuit in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 興化瀕海，鎮將所部皆群盜受撫者。

translations.literal: Xinghua bordered the sea; those under the regional commander were all bandit gangs who had accepted pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Xinghua lay on the coast, and the commander's troops were mostly formerly pacified pirate bands.

sentences.zh: 有材官辱張氏僕，張氏以告。

translations.literal: A skilled-officer insulted a Zhang household servant; the Zhang family reported it.
translations.idiomatic: An officer insulted a servant of the Zhang family, who lodged a complaint.

sentences.zh: 鎮將撻材官，部卒大譁，毀張氏之室，欲劫鎮將為亂。

translations.literal: The regional commander flogged the skilled-officer; the troops clamored loudly, destroyed the Zhang residence, and wished to seize the commander and make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The commander had the officer flogged, whereupon the troops rioted, wrecked the Zhang home, and nearly seized their commander in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 鎮將避去，則縊被撻者寘張氏，謂其僕殺之。

translations.literal: The regional commander avoided the place; then they hanged the man who had been flogged and placed him at the Zhang household, claiming their servant had killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The commander fled; the mutineers hanged the flogged officer at the Zhang residence and accused their servant of murder.

sentences.zh: 朋舉甫到官，廉得首惡，猝縛至，集文武吏會鞫，健兒帶刀環立瞋視。

translations.literal: Pengju had just arrived in office; through investigation he got the chief culprits and suddenly bound them and brought them forth; he gathered civil and military officials for joint trial, while braves with swords stood around glaring.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju had only just taken office; he identified the ringleaders, seized them at once, and convened civil and military officials for trial while armed soldiers glared from every side.

sentences.zh: 朋舉從容曰：「若曹幹軍法，罪重。

translations.literal: Pengju said calmly: "You have violated military law—the offense is grave.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju said calmly, "You have violated military law—a grave offense."

sentences.zh: 念若曹約束無素，但用殺人律，罪有專屬。

translations.literal: Considering that you lack regular discipline, apply only the statute on homicide—guilt has its proper owner.
translations.idiomatic: "But given your undisciplined conduct, apply only the homicide statute—guilt rests with whoever actually killed him."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃泥首，言殺人者為張氏僕。

translations.literal: The crowd then pressed their foreheads to the ground, saying the killer was the Zhang household servant.
translations.idiomatic: The troops kowtowed and claimed the Zhang servant was the killer.

sentences.zh: 朋舉曰：「若曹氣焰何等，彼能於千百健兒中奪一人縊之耶？

translations.literal: Pengju said: "What sort of spirit were you people—could he seize one man from among a thousand braves and hang him?
translations.idiomatic: Pengju asked, "With your numbers and ferocity, could a household servant seize one of you from your midst and hang him?"

sentences.zh: 」召訊證者，俱吐實，誅三人而事定。

translations.literal: He summoned witnesses for questioning; all confessed the truth; three men were executed and the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He called witnesses, all confessed, three men were executed, and the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 泉州提督剿海盜，盜逸入興化界，鎮將獲數百人。

translations.literal: The Quanzhou naval commander suppressed sea pirates; the pirates fled into the Xinghua border, and the regional commander captured several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Quanzhou naval commander drove sea pirates inland, the regional commander seized several hundred men in Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 朋舉視其嘗薙發者，曰：「此良民被陷，當宥。

translations.literal: Pengju looked at those who had once shaved their heads and said: "These are good people who were trapped—they should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing those who had once shaved their heads in the Ming style, he said, "These are innocent people framed—they should be spared."

sentences.zh: 」有年少者，曰：「童穉何知，又當宥。

translations.literal: Where there were younger ones, he said: "What do children know—they too should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Of the younger captives he said, "Children know nothing of such matters—spare them too."

sentences.zh: 」全活甚眾。

translations.literal: A great many lives were entirely preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 鄭成功屯廈門，與漳州隔海相望。

translations.literal: Zheng Chenggong was stationed at Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held Xiamen, facing Zhangzhou across the strait.

sentences.zh: 固山額真駐會城，遣兵戍漳州，番代歲四易，民苦供役。

translations.literal: The banner general-in-chief was stationed at the provincial capital and sent troops to garrison Zhangzhou; rotations changed four times a year, and the people suffered from supplying corvée.
translations.idiomatic: A banner general at the provincial capital garrisoned Zhangzhou with troops rotated four times a year, and the people groaned under the burden of supply.

sentences.zh: 朋舉請駐防無屢更，不許；

translations.literal: Pengju requested that garrison rotations not change frequently; this was not granted;
translations.idiomatic: Pengju asked that the garrison not rotate so often; his request was denied;

sentences.zh: 固請展其期，歲再易，民稍蘇息。

translations.literal: he urgently requested extending the term; rotations came twice a year, and the people gradually found relief.
translations.idiomatic: he pressed to extend the rotation interval to twice a year, and the people found some relief.

sentences.zh: 擢四川按察使、山東右布政使。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Sichuan surveillance commissioner and right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan and Right Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起授湖南布政使。

translations.literal: Upon recall he was appointed administration commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled from mourning he was appointed Administration Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 上官，見胥吏至數百，曰：「兵初罷，民方重困。

translations.literal: On taking office he saw clerks numbering several hundred and said: "The troops have just stood down; the people are now in heavy distress.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he saw hundreds of clerks and said, "The war has just ended and the people are still desperately poor."

sentences.zh: 此曹鮮衣美食，縱橫市井間，何所​​取諸？

translations.literal: These fellows in fresh clothes and fine food swagger through the market streets—where do they get it?
translations.idiomatic: "Yet these men dress well, eat well, and swagger through the markets—where does it all come from?"

sentences.zh: 」汰其十九，擇謹願者，取足供文書而已。

translations.literal: He eliminated nineteen out of twenty, chose the respectful and willing, and took only enough to handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed nineteen out of twenty, kept only the most conscientious, and retained just enough staff for paperwork.

sentences.zh: 數為大吏言地方利病，有司賢不肖積與之忤，被劾鐫級，未行，而大吏以貪敗。

translations.literal: He repeatedly spoke to high officials on the benefits and harms of the locality; over time he clashed with worthy and unworthy officials alike, was impeached and had his rank carved down; before he departed, the high official fell through greed.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly reported local problems to his superiors, clashed with good and bad officials alike, was impeached and demoted—and before he could leave, his accuser was himself ruined for corruption.

sentences.zh: 士民惜之。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and commoners mourned his departure.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: =王天鑑=王天鑑，字近微，直隸萬全人。

translations.literal: Wang Tianjian—courtesy name Jinwei—was a native of Wanquan in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tianjian, styled Jinwei, was from Wanquan in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授山東恩縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed magistrate of En county in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 縣接直隸界，自明季為盜藪，嘗一歲七被寇。

translations.literal: The county adjoined the Zhili border; since the late Ming it had been a bandit den and once suffered seven raids in a single year.
translations.idiomatic: The county bordered Zhili and had been a bandit haven since the late Ming; one year it was raided seven times.

sentences.zh: 天鑑上官，諭父老曰：「往歲寇至，縣輒不守，由人無固志。

translations.literal: When Tianjian took office he instructed the elders: "In past years when bandits came the county was always abandoned, because people lacked firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he told the elders, "In past years when bandits came the county was abandoned because people lost heart."

sentences.zh: 自今勿復逃，視知縣所向。

translations.literal: From now on do not flee again—watch where the magistrate goes.
translations.idiomatic: "From now on do not flee—follow where your magistrate leads."

sentences.zh: 」俄而寇大至，天鑑坐城上，從容指揮，寇疑有伏，逡巡去。

translations.literal: Soon bandits came in great force; Tianjian sat atop the city wall and directed affairs calmly; the bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: When a large bandit force arrived, Tianjian sat on the city wall and directed the defense calmly; the raiders suspected an ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是葺樓櫓，治城隍，嚴候望，時巡徼，守具大備。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired towers and battlements, restored the moat and walls, tightened watch posts, patrolled regularly, and defensive preparations were fully complete.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired towers and walls, restored the moat, tightened watches, patrolled regularly, and made the defenses complete.

sentences.zh: 按行鄉鄙，舉團練，立砦十有九，枹鼓相聞，久之得步卒萬八千、騎士三百。

translations.literal: Making inspection rounds through villages and outskirts, he raised militia, established nineteen stockades with drum and gong signals linking them; in time he had eighteen thousand infantry and three hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Touring the countryside he organized militia, built nineteen stockades with linked drum signals, and eventually mustered eighteen thousand foot soldiers and three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史疏聞，令天鑑自治兵。

translations.literal: The touring censor memorialized report and ordered Tianjian to command troops himself.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor reported his work, and the court authorized Tianjian to command local forces himself.

sentences.zh: 廉得境內賊渠數輩，夜突至其鄉呼之出，賊錯愕不能遁，皆誅之。

translations.literal: Through investigation he learned of several bandit chiefs within the district; at night he burst into their villages calling them out; the bandits, startled and unable to escape, were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: He identified several local bandit leaders, raided their villages by night, caught them before they could flee, and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 寇據曹縣，巡撫檄天鑑與諸道兵會剿，率所部為前鋒，冒矢石深入，諸軍踵之，復其城。

translations.literal: Bandits occupied Caoxian; the governor-general ordered Tianjian and troops of various circuits to join in suppression; he led his own forces as vanguard, braved arrows and stones in deep advance, other armies followed, and the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized Caoxian, the governor ordered a joint campaign; Tianjian led his men as vanguard, charged through arrow fire, and the combined force retook the city.

sentences.zh: 嘗以輕騎逐賊，日暮被圍，短兵相接，手格殺數賊，潰圍出，不失一騎。

translations.literal: Once with light cavalry he pursued bandits; at dusk he was surrounded, fought hand-to-hand at close quarters, killed several bandits with his own hands, broke through the encirclement, and did not lose a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Once, pursuing bandits with light cavalry, he was surrounded at dusk; fighting hand to hand he killed several raiders, broke through, and did not lose a single trooper.

sentences.zh: 在恩四年，屢與寇戰，俘馘無算，降者安撫之。

translations.literal: During four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly; captives and slain heads were beyond counting; those who surrendered he pacified and comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Over four years at En he fought bandits repeatedly, took countless prisoners and heads, and pacified those who surrendered.

sentences.zh: 寇遠遁，招徠屯種，流亡復歸，墾荒千八百頃。

translations.literal: The bandits fled far away; he summoned people to settle and farm; displaced persons returned; wasteland reclaimed reached eighteen hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits fled he encouraged settlement and farming; refugees returned and nearly two thousand qing of wasteland was brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 建書院，弦誦不輟。

translations.literal: He built an academy; recitation of the classics did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy where study never ceased.

sentences.zh: 政聲為山東最，上考，內遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: His administrative reputation was foremost in Shandong; in the top evaluation he was transferred inward to a director post in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was the finest in Shandong; rated top in evaluation he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十一年，始行耤田親耕禮，天鑑參酌古今，悉合禮宜。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field by the emperor in person was first performed; Tianjian drew on past and present and all conformed to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the emperor first performed the sacred-field plowing ceremony in person, Tianjian coordinated the rites from historical precedent and all passed muster.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose steadily to Director in the ministry.

sentences.zh: 主山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He presided over the Shandong provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Shandong provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出為陝西河西道參議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out to serve as junior vice prefect of the Hexi circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was posted as Junior Vice Prefect of the Hexi Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與屬吏約，毋獵民枉法。

translations.literal: He made an agreement with subordinate officials not to hunt the people or twist the law.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged to his staff not to prey on the people or pervert the law.

sentences.zh: 天鑑固長治兵，按籍討軍實，誡將弁毋以軍糈肥私橐。

translations.literal: Tianjian was skilled at governing troops; he checked registers to verify military strength and admonished officers not to fatten private purses with army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian had long excelled at military affairs; he audited troop rolls and warned officers not to fill private purses from army rations.

sentences.zh: 性剛介負氣，數忤上官。

translations.literal: By nature he was stiff and self-respecting, with proud spirit, and repeatedly offended superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and proud by nature, he often clashed with his superiors.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，謝病歸。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he cited illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 絕跡公府，門下士或有餽遺，不受，曰：「飭簠簋，惜名節，足以報舉主矣！

translations.literal: He cut off all contact with government offices; when students under his gate sometimes made gifts he did not accept, saying: "To keep one's vessels in order and cherish one's name and integrity is enough to repay one's recommender!
translations.idiomatic: He avoided official circles entirely; when students offered gifts he refused them, saying, "Guarding one's integrity is repayment enough to those who recommended you!"

sentences.zh: 」康熙初，大臣薦，不出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi ministers recommended him, but he did not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign ministers recommended him, but he would not serve again.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: =趙廷標=趙廷標，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingbiao was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingbiao was from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，以拔貢生授福建永定知縣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, as a selected tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Yongding in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 廣東大埔逸寇江龍以萬餘人犯縣城，廷標城守。

translations.literal: The fugitive bandit Jiang Long of Dapu in Guangdong invaded the prefectural city with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao defended the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Long, a rebel leader from Dapu in Guangdong, attacked the county seat with more than ten thousand men; Tingbiao held the walls.

sentences.zh: 寇穴地入，瀦池水以待，地砲不得發；

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled underground to enter; he dammed pool water in readiness, so that land mines could not be fired;
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tunneled under the walls; he flooded the moats so underground powder charges could not be fired;

sentences.zh: 樹雲梯乘城，於城上懸柵墮之。

translations.literal: they set scaling ladders to climb the wall; he hung palisades from atop the wall to drop on them.
translations.idiomatic: they raised scaling ladders; he hung timber barriers from the battlements to drop on them.

sentences.zh: 持三月，食垂盡。

translations.literal: They held out three months until food was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three months until food was nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 值立春，廷標張鼓樂，開城門，迎春東郊。

translations.literal: When the Beginning of Spring arrived, Tingbiao displayed drums and music, opened the city gates, and welcomed spring in the eastern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: At the Beginning of Spring, Tingbiao staged drums and music, opened the gates, and went out to the eastern suburbs for the spring ritual.

sentences.zh: 寇疑有伏，引去。

translations.literal: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits suspected an ambush and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 密遣兵間道往伏兩山間，出不意夾擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He secretly sent troops by hidden paths to lie in wait between two mountains, struck from unexpected quarters in a pincer attack, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent troops along hidden paths to ambush them between the hills and routed them in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 進至龍磜寨，捕斬略盡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Longji stockade, he captured and beheaded nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Longji stockade, he captured and executed most of the survivors.

sentences.zh: 擢湖廣衡州同知，署府事。

translations.literal: He was elevated to sub-prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and acted as prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Sub-Prefect of Hengzhou in Huguang and served as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 蠲賦墾荒，流亡復業。

translations.literal: He remitted taxes, reclaimed wasteland, and displaced persons returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted taxes, encouraged reclaiming wasteland, and brought refugees back to their farms.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，賑恤有實惠。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine his relief and succor had real benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe famine his relief reached people with real effect.

sentences.zh: 經略大學士洪承疇薦廷標，十七年，擢雲南迤東道副使。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou as frontier commissioner recommended Tingbiao; in the seventeenth year he was elevated to vice prefect of the Yidong circuit in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou recommended him; in the seventeenth year he was made Vice Prefect of the Yidong Circuit in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 安普諸番為土官所誘，競作不靖。

translations.literal: Various tribes of Anpu were incited by native officials and competed in making unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Various tribal peoples of the Anpu region, incited by native officials, rose in succession.

sentences.zh: 廷標設方略、行間，解散之，遂復維摩舊地。

translations.literal: Tingbiao devised strategy and used secret agents to dissolve them, and thereby recovered the old territory of Weimo.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbiao devised strategy and used agents to break them up, and thereby recovered the old Weimo territory.

sentences.zh: 移檄諭寧州彌勒、巴盤、八甸，罷捕逐之令，令諸持田器者皆為良民，持兵者乃為賊。

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to instruct Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, abolishing orders to hunt and drive them out, decreeing that all who held farming tools were good people and only those who held weapons were bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations to Ningzhou, Mile, Bapan, and Badian, ending the policy of hunting tribesmen down: whoever held farming tools was a loyal subject; only those bearing arms were treated as rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡行安撫，諸路悉平。

translations.literal: Making inspection rounds to pacify and comfort, all routes were entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the region to pacify the people, and every district was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 治迤東十八年。

translations.literal: He governed Yidong for eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the Yidong region for eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，調廣東廣肇南韶道副使。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he was transferred to be vice commissioner of the Guangzhaonan Shao circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Guangzhaonan Shao Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 安普民、蠻聞其去，塹道塞城留之。

translations.literal: When the people and tribes of Anpu heard he was leaving, they dug ditches across the roads and blocked the city to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: When the people and tribes of Anpu heard he was leaving, they dug ditches across the roads and blocked the city gates to keep him from going.

sentences.zh: 慰諭再三，乃得行。

translations.literal: After comforting and instructing them again and again, he was finally able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Only after repeated reassurances was he able to leave.

sentences.zh: 兩粵八排諸山寇聞廷標來，望風解散。

translations.literal: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in the two Guang provinces heard Tingbiao was coming, they dispersed at the report of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: When the mountain bandits of the Eight Ranks in Guangdong and Guangxi heard Tingbiao was coming, they dispersed at the news.

sentences.zh: 連州亂，至，立就撫。

translations.literal: When Lianzhou was in disorder, upon his arrival they immediately submitted to pacification.
translations.idiomatic: When Lianzhou rebelled, he arrived and the rebels submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 逾年以憂去。

translations.literal: After more than a year he left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he went home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起湖南驛鹽道副使。

translations.literal: Upon recall he was appointed vice commissioner of the courier and salt circuit in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Courier and Salt Circuit in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 捕治劇寇，誅其渠，餘悉縱歸農。

translations.literal: He captured and punished fierce bandits, executed their leaders, and released the rest all to return to farming.
translations.idiomatic: He captured major bandits, executed their leaders, and released the rest to return to farming.

sentences.zh: 湖南方用兵，芻茭械仗，儲峙供給，不誤晷刻，民不困役。

translations.literal: Hunan was then employing troops; fodder, weapons, and equipment were stored in readiness for supply without missing a single moment, and the people were not distressed by corvée.
translations.idiomatic: With Hunan at war, he stockpiled fodder, weapons, and equipment and met every deadline without burdening the people with excessive levies.

sentences.zh: 兼攝糧道。

translations.literal: He also held concurrent charge of the grain transport circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會湘東民變，巡撫韓世琦令廷標往撫之。

translations.literal: When the people of eastern Hunan rose in disorder, Governor Han Shiqi ordered Tingbiao to go pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Hunan erupted in unrest, Governor Han Shiqi sent Tingbiao to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 單騎馳諭，皆悔泣聽命，散遣之。

translations.literal: Riding alone at speed he went to instruct them; all repented and wept as they obeyed, and he dispersed and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out alone to reason with them; they wept in repentance, obeyed his orders, and were sent home.

sentences.zh: 事稍定，修岳麓書院，置田禀諸生。

translations.literal: When affairs were somewhat settled, he repaired the Yuelu Academy and set aside fields to supply the students.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored he restored the Yuelu Academy and endowed fields to support its students.

sentences.zh: 嘗行部至衡州，父老羅拜車下，號以「慈母」。

translations.literal: Once when making an inspection tour to Hengzhou, elders lined up to bow below his carriage and called him the "Kind Mother."
translations.idiomatic: Once on an inspection tour to Hengzhou, elders lined the road to bow before his carriage and hailed him as their "kind mother."

sentences.zh: 俄遷陝西糧儲道參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be junior vice prefect of the grain storage circuit in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Junior Vice Prefect of the Grain Storage Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 已病，值武昌兵變，軍書至，猶強起視事。

translations.literal: He was already ill; when the military mutiny at Wuchang occurred and military dispatches arrived, he still forced himself to rise and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Already ill, when the Wuchang mutiny broke out and urgent dispatches arrived, he still dragged himself to his desk.

sentences.zh: 病篤乞歸，至家卒。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave and he begged to return home; upon reaching home he died.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened and he begged to go home; he died soon after arriving.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：自置督撫，而兩司權輕，況於各道；

translations.literal: Commentary says: Since governors-general and governors were established, the two provincial commissions grew light in authority—how much more so the circuit offices;
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Once governors-general and governors were installed, the provincial commissions lost weight—and circuit offices even more so;

sentences.zh: 然以賢者處之，奉職循理，視民之所急，弭亂解嬈，亦足以為治。

translations.literal: yet when men of worth hold such posts, fulfilling duty according to principle, regarding what the people urgently need, quelling disorder and relieving harassment, that too is sufficient for good government.
translations.idiomatic: yet when capable men hold such posts, perform their duties conscientiously, address what the people need most, and quell unrest, that is government enough.

sentences.zh: 而述、振芬、振姬、天鑑皆有才略，根本尤在廉勤。

translations.literal: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and strategy; the foundation lay especially in integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: Ershu, Zhenfen, Zhenji, and Tianjian all had talent and drive; above all they were rooted in integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 延著、國棟、廷標當治亂用重之日，濟之以寬仁，雖以是罷貶，甚或中危法，而一不自卹，是皆能舉其職者。

translations.literal: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao lived in days when order and disorder called for stern measures; they supplemented this with leniency and kindness; though some were dismissed and demoted for it, and some even fell under perilous statutes, not one spared himself—these all were men who could fulfill their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhu, Guodong, and Tingbiao served in times that demanded force; they tempered it with mercy. Some were demoted or even faced capital charges, yet none spared themselves—all fulfilled their duty.

sentences.zh: 澤及於斯民，亦已多矣。

translations.literal: The blessings reaching these people were already many.
translations.idiomatic: The good they did for the people was already beyond measure.
